questions.question: Which description most accurately defines shock?

choices.text: Inadequate cellular perfusion, which may exist before blood pressure falls
Any low blood-pressure reading, regardless of cellular perfusion
A rapid pulse that always indicates blood loss
Reduced oxygen in the lungs with otherwise adequate tissue delivery

questions.explanation: Shock concerns inadequate perfusion of cells, not one isolated vital sign or a single cause.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Blood pressure must be interpreted with perfusion findings; it is not the entire definition.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Tachycardia is neither a definition nor proof of blood loss.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Lung oxygenation and tissue perfusion are related but distinct.

questions.question: Which set correctly matches the three parts of the perfusion triangle?

choices.text: Heart: pump; vessels: container; blood: contents
Heart: container; vessels: contents; blood: pump
Heart: contents; lungs: pump; vessels: container

incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: The heart is the pump; the lungs do not replace it in this triangle.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Lungs and glucose do not replace vessels and circulating blood.

questions.question: Why can shock injure cells even when waste products are still being produced normally?

choices.text: Reduced blood flow delays transport of wastes away from tissues
Reduced blood flow raises the rate of waste removal above its production
Adequate ventilation clears tissue wastes even when their blood transport is impaired
Normal waste production means clearance remains adequate despite reduced flow

questions.explanation: Inadequate perfusion compromises clearance as well as delivery, allowing damaging waste accumulation.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Reduced flow impairs removal rather than accelerating it.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Wastes must reach the lungs through blood flow.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Production and clearance are separate processes.

questions.question: A patient’s blood pressure is 102/82 mm Hg. What is the pulse pressure, and how should it be interpreted in the shock assessment?

choices.text: 20 mm Hg; narrow pulse pressure
82 mm Hg; narrow pulse pressure
102 mm Hg; wide pulse pressure
184 mm Hg; wide pulse pressure

questions.explanation: Pulse pressure is systolic minus diastolic: 102 − 82 = 20. A value below 25 may occur in shock but is not a standalone diagnosis.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: 82 is the diastolic pressure, not the difference.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: 102 is the systolic pressure.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Pulse pressure is the difference, not the sum.

Provide oxygen and use improvement in oxygen saturation to decide whether rapid transport remains necessary.
Provide oxygen, complete the full secondary examination on scene, and then arrange transport.

archivedQuestions.explanation: Tamponade restricts cardiac filling and can cause obstructive shock. Oxygen and other EMT support help sustain the patient, but definitive treatment requires surgery. incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Additional examination should be rapid and can continue en route. Completing the full examination on scene should not delay transport of a deteriorating shock patient.
